sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the outages and the strikes] Russian overnight strikes on energy facilities left more than 600,000 people without power in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region (Pavlohrad, Samarivskyi, Kamianske, Dnipro districts and Dnipro city) and nearly 250,000 in the Kharkiv region on Sunday Nov 8; Ukrenergo imposed emergency power outages in Kharkiv, Sumy and Poltava regions. Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces will continue striking fuel and energy infrastructure it says aids Ukraine's military, and said it also struck a container ship south-west of Odesa. Total without power ~850,000 (AJ headline figure).
sections.what_verified: 2 independent publisher families: AFP (T1 wire) and Al Jazeera (T2). DTEK's Telegram post is the primary source for its own outage figures; DTEK is unregistered in the source-registry so it does not count toward corroboration but is reported with attribution. AFP syndicated copies (Straits Times, Gulf Today, Channels TV, Bangkok Post, FMT, Centreline, edition.mv, NN24, Rapporteur) count as ONE family. UNN (Ukrenergo) corroborates emergency outages but UNN is unregistered, so it does not count.
sections.what_disputed: Russia MoD: strikes target energy facilities used to aid Ukraine's military; Russia says the Odesa container ship carried weapons/military equipment -- cargo claim unverified. Zelenskyy (per Rapporteur) said the death toll has risen to 55 -- scope of that figure is unclear (not tied to this specific strike in the reporting), treat as his claim, not a verified toll for this attack. Note: this is a NEW Sunday overnight attack, distinct from Saturday Nov 7's Kyiv barrage (36 ballistic missiles, Northern Bridge) covered in earlier scans; the 1600 scan missed the AFP original (09:09Z = 13:09 ) -- this is a missed catch-up surfaced in-window via AnewZ 16:38 / AJ 16:20 .
sections.why_matters: 850,000 in the dark -- Russia hits Ukraine's power grid 48 hours before the Abu Dhabi talks; only 4 of 36 ballistic missiles were stopped on Saturday
